html:
Proto-Tibetan cultures is the map's label for the peoples of the Tibetan Plateau around 400 BCE, before any of them left written records. Little is known for certain about them.

Archaeology shows Iron Age villages and stone tombs. People grew barley in the sheltered river valleys and herded yaks, sheep and goats on the high pastures. In the west this world produced the kingdom of Zhangzhung; in the south it led to the Yarlung kings, who later built the Tibetan Empire. They were the ancestors of later Tibetans.
sum: Proto-Tibetan cultures is the map's label for the peoples of the Tibetan Plateau around 400 BCE, before any of them left written records. Little is known for certain about them.
